correctness.rationale: The unique 1 makes every necklace primitive and canonically gives three nonnegative zero gaps. Rows starting in zeros first sort by decreasing leading-zero length, then by the next nonzero letter; for the two rows with next letter 2, the comparison is b versus c and at equality the B row reaches 1 first. The same tie-break applies to the marker-start rows. A gap contributes its nonzero predecessor on its first active level only; further levels at a constant active set contribute zeros, so one zero preserves all run boundaries for two or more levels. The multiplicities give a geometric factor for each repeated active-set size. Independently, I used all weak rankings of the three gaps with zero allowed and with adjacent positive length increments either 1 or at least 2. I sorted the literal rotations of each representative and used integer polynomial arithmetic to reproduce every numerator over (1-z)(1-z^2)(1-z^3) in exactly 111 cases; I also enumerated and sorted all rotations at each length 3–54 as a finite cross-check. For positivity, F3 has denominator 1-z^6 and numerator z^4(2+2z+z^2+3z^3+z^4+2z^5), F5=zF3/(1-z), F4 has positive numerator z^4(1+2z+3z^2) over (1-z^2)(1-z^3), and F6 has a z^6 contribution with denominator containing 1-z. Contributions below six runs grow at most linearly, versus quadratically many necklaces.
residual_risks: The finite direct enumeration is a cross-check; all-length validity uses the rotation-order and zero-block invariance argument. Results concern ordinary linear runs only, not cyclic runs or sentinel-based BWT.

evidence: The permutation theorem is general in the Parikh vector but does not enumerate by run count. Simpson–Puglisi characterize a descending three-block output. The general sparse-weight law addressed binary words, bounding runs by 2k and establishing a sufficient-gap family and an asymptotic.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The descending-block result can intersect only a portion of the three-run stratum; the binary bound and typical behavior cannot supply the mixed-marker ternary all-stratum frequencies.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: To derive these frequencies still requires a run-refined enumeration. In particular, the b/c tie-break and whether simultaneous levels separate nonzero predecessors from each other and the marker-start rows are needed for the odd and even classes; they are not consequences of the descending case or the general fixed-content inversion alone.

evidence: The unique marker gives a bijection between the assigned necklaces and nonnegative zero-gap triples. By primitive BWT inversion the same census counts last columns of the fixed content whose LF map is one cycle, stratified by the number of linear runs. Crochemore–Désarménien–Perrin give the inverse/permutation relation and a fixed-Parikh-vector bijection, not counts of this run statistic.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Neither rephrasing as color-gap vectors nor as single-cycle LF permutations removes the run constraint. Binary identical markers are not equivalent under letter relabeling to the ordered mixed-marker content.

value.rationale: BWT runs are the statistic used in run-length compression; this is a natural first sparse ternary extension of the three-marker binary family, with just one marker changing letter. The complete generating functions quantify which run values persist at every length, how often each exceptional value occurs, and the concentration on six runs. This gives a reusable fixed-content benchmark rather than a single example of an odd run count.
residual_risks: No universal ternary compression or asymptotic claim for other compositions is supported.
